text: In courts, a versatility of genius and softness of manners are absolutely necessary; which some people mistake for abject flattery, and having no opinion of one's own; whereas it is only the decent and genteel manner of maintaining your own opinion, and possibly of bringing other people to it.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XXXVIII, to his son, London, May 10, Old Style 1748
